intro: Guatemala City rewards visitors with its vibrant markets, rich history, and lively food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Transmetro BRT: 7 lines, use Citizen's Card (Q20 with 5 trips) or contactless card; cash not accepted.
Transurbano buses: prepaid card needed; slower but more routes.
Red city buses are unsafe; avoid.
Taxis: yellow metered (call 1766) or white negotiate price; Uber works.
Driving: chaotic traffic; rental cars available but not recommended for city driving.
Walking: use caution; accompanied walking advised.

national-palace.name: National Palace of Culture
national-palace.landmark: National Palace of Culture, Guatemala City
national-palace.price_text: Free entry; bring photo ID for registration — check on the day
national-palace.hours: Tue–Sun daytime; closed Monday — check on the day
national-palace.tip: Join a free guided tour of the state rooms and inner courtyards. Bring your passport.

metropolitan-cathedral.name: Metropolitan Cathedral
metropolitan-cathedral.price_text: Free; small fee for some crypt areas
metropolitan-cathedral.hours: Daily, roughly 07:00–18:00 — check on the day
metropolitan-cathedral.tip: Look for the old crypts beneath the floor; the plaza outside is lively and worth a slow loop.

kaminaljuyu.name: Kaminaljuyu
kaminaljuyu.price_text: Small entry fee — check on the day
kaminaljuyu.hours: Daytime, closed some days — check on the day
kaminaljuyu.tip: This is a grassy mound site inside the city, not a big ruin complex. Set expectations low and enjoy the quiet.

arqueologia-museum.name: Museo Nacional de Arqueología y Etnología
arqueologia-museum.landmark: Museo Nacional de Arqueología y Etnología
arqueologia-museum.price_text: Modest entry fee; discounts for students — check on the day
arqueologia-museum.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday — check on the day
arqueologia-museum.tip: Start with the Maya stelae and the Tikal models. Labels are mostly Spanish.

popol-vuh.name: Popol Vuh Museum
popol-vuh.price_text: Entry fee — check on the day
popol-vuh.hours: Mon–Fri and some Saturdays — check on the day
popol-vuh.tip: Small but excellent Maya ceramics collection on a university campus. Ask the guard for directions to the entrance.

antigua.name: Antigua Guatemala day trip
antigua.price_text: Transport and tours vary widely — check on the day
antigua.hours: Day trip; leave early to beat traffic
antigua.tip: About an hour from the city when traffic is kind. Go early and plan to stay for lunch.

cerro-cruz.name: Hill of the Cross (Cerro de la Cruz)
cerro-cruz.landmark: Hill of the Cross (Cerro de la Cruz)
cerro-cruz.price_text: Free; small tip for parking helpers
cerro-cruz.tip: Best view of Antigua and the volcanoes. Go with a group and avoid walking up alone after dark.

ixchel.name: Ixchel Museum of Indigenous Textiles
ixchel.price_text: Entry fee — check on the day
ixchel.hours: Mon–Fri, some Saturdays — check on the day
ixchel.tip: The huipil collection explains regional dress patterns. A good rainy-afternoon stop.

la-merced.name: La Merced Church
la-merced.price_text: Free; small fee for the cloister
la-merced.hours: Daily daytime — check on the day
la-merced.tip: The yellow facade is the classic Antigua photo. Visit in the morning for softer light.

mundo-petapa.name: Mundo Petapa Theme Park
mundo-petapa.price_text: Ride tickets or day pass — check on the day
mundo-petapa.hours: Weekends and holidays mainly — check on the day
mundo-petapa.tip: A family day out with rides and pools. Confirm opening days before you go.

capitanes.name: Palacio de los Capitanes Generales
capitanes.price_text: Entry varies by exhibition — check on the day
capitanes.hours: Daytime, some closures — check on the day
capitanes.tip: On Antigua's main plaza. Combine with the cathedral and a coffee nearby.

pepian.name: Pepián tasting
pepian.price_text: Main dish roughly GTQ 60–120 — check on the day
pepian.hours: Lunch and dinner at most traditional restaurants
pepian.tip: A thick, spiced stew — try it at a traditional comedor rather than a tourist spot.

san-francisco.name: San Francisco Church
san-francisco.price_text: Free; small fee for the museum and tomb
san-francisco.hours: Daily daytime — check on the day
san-francisco.tip: Home of the Santo Hermano Pedro. Quiet, working church — dress respectfully.

santa-catalina.name: Santa Catalina Arch
santa-catalina.hours: Always visible; street busy all day
santa-catalina.tip: The most photographed spot in Antigua. Come early to get a shot without crowds.

mercado-central.name: Mercado Central
mercado-central.price_text: Free to enter; meals roughly GTQ 25–60
mercado-central.hours: Daily, roughly 06:00–18:00 — check on the day
mercado-central.tip: Go for a cheap set lunch at the comedores upstairs. Keep valuables close.

zona-4-walk.name: Zona 4 neighbourhood walk
zona-4-walk.tip: Cafés, galleries and street art. Walk by day and take a taxi back at night.

zona-10-walk.name: Zona 10 dining and shopping walk
zona-10-walk.tip: The safest and most polished district for an easy first evening. Many restaurants and malls.

city-tour.name: Guided historic centre walking tour
city-tour.price_text: ≈ GTQ 100–250 per person — check on the day
city-tour.tip: A guide makes Zona 1 much easier to read. Book ahead and confirm the meeting point.

relief-map.name: Relief map viewpoint (Mapa en Relieve)
relief-map.price_text: Small entry fee — check on the day
relief-map.tip: A giant scale model of Guatemala's mountains. Good for understanding the country's geography.

airport-food.name: Comedor lunch near the centre
airport-food.tip: Look for a busy local comedor for a cheap, filling set lunch. Ask what's fresh.

stays.why: Modern, safest-feeling base. Hotels, restaurants and malls within walking distance; easy taxi and ride-app pickups.
Next to Zona 10 and the Torre del Reformador area. Quieter streets, still close to dining and nightlife.
Historic center: Plaza Mayor, the cathedral and the National Palace. Cheapest, but use care on foot, especially after dark.
Trendy, walkable pocket of cafés, bars and galleries. Good for nightlife and food; book ahead on weekends.

food: Try Guatemalan staples: pepián (thick spiced stew), kak'ik (turkey soup), tamales and chuchitos.
Mercado Central in Zona 1: cheap comedores and fresh produce. Go with a local or in a group; keep valuables out of sight.
Breakfast: eggs, black beans, plantain and thick tortillas. Cafés in Zona 4 and Zona 10 do good coffee.
Street snacks: tostadas, shucos (hot dogs with toppings) and rellenitos (plantain with bean paste). Eat where locals queue.
Prices vary. Budget roughly Q30–80 for a simple meal and Q150+ at mid-range restaurants. Check the bill for service charges.
more_time: Swap a city day for Antigua Guatemala: colonial streets and volcano views, roughly an hour by road. Check bus and shuttle times on the day.
Add Lake Atitlán or Chichicastenango market as an overnight, not a day trip. Roads are slow; book a shuttle.
Maya history fans: the Museo Nacional de Arqueología y Etnología in Zona 13 pairs well with a half-day at the relief map (Mapa en Relieve) in Zona 2.
